options: A journal entry where only a debit (or credit) was posted, with no matching credit (or debit) entered
A journal entry with exactly one debit and one credit
An entry that only affects revenue accounts
An entry that has already been reversed
questions.explain: A one-sided entry means one side of the double-entry pair was never recorded, which will throw the trial balance out of balance.

questions.q: If a trial balance's difference divides evenly by 9, what type of error does that suggest?
options: A missing journal entry with no error otherwise
A transposition error, where two digits were swapped while keying an amount
A duplicate payment to a vendor
An error that can never actually be diagnosed
questions.explain: Transposition errors (swapping two adjacent digits) always produce a difference evenly divisible by 9.

questions.q: If a trial balance's difference divides evenly by 2, what should you check for?
options: A revenue recognition timing issue
Whether the company changed its fiscal year
Whether depreciation was calculated incorrectly
Whether an amount was posted entirely to the wrong side instead of correctly offsetting the other side
questions.explain: When an amount is posted to the wrong side entirely rather than split correctly, the resulting imbalance is exactly double that amount.

questions.q: Westbridge Consulting Group's trial balance is off by $90. What is the first diagnostic step suggested by this lesson?
options: Immediately re-enter every transaction from the entire year
Assume the trial balance report itself is broken and ignore the issue
Check whether $90 divides evenly by 9 or by 2 to narrow down the likely type of error
Delete the most recent journal entry without reviewing it
questions.explain: Dividing the imbalance by 9 and by 2 are the fast first checks that narrow down the likely cause before manually re-checking every entry.

questions.q: Why is this troubleshooting mindset relevant to real Oracle Fusion support work?
options: Because imbalances can still arise from manual entries, data conversion during implementation, or integration issues, and recognizing classic error patterns speeds up diagnosis
Because modern ERP systems can never have an imbalance
Because Oracle Fusion does not use trial balances at all
Because this knowledge is only useful for paper-based bookkeeping, not modern systems
questions.explain: Even in automated systems, imbalances can occur, and a consultant who recognizes classic error patterns can diagnose issues much faster.
